about: Simplified Technical English wording for the visible sentences of the main page, Tools and Planner data files (Moon part). The old sentence is the key; the new sentence keeps its meaning and numbers.

copy.json.For choosing where and when to rehearse: Use this page to find where and when to rehearse rover operations, camera tests and crew work under the light of the Moon's south pole.
copy.json.A map and a calendar of the places and d: A map and a calendar show the places and dates where the Sun stays that low over bare, snow-free ground. These places copy the height of the Sun and the length of the shadows. They do not copy the strong contrast of a world without air.

glossary.json.An unbroken stretch of time with the Sun: A time without a break in which the Sun is above the horizon and below the Sun ceiling of a lunar region. We count spells of 2 hours or more.
glossary.json.One of the 36 parts of our year, ten day: One of the 36 parts of our year. Each part has 10 days, from 1 Jan. The last part has 15 days, to complete the year.
glossary.json.The highest the Sun climbs at a lunar re: The highest angle of the Sun at a lunar region, in degrees above a level horizon. It is 2.08 degrees at Connecting Ridge and 7.90 degrees at Peak near Cabeus B.
glossary.json.The line where land meets sky, seen from: The line where the land meets the sky, as seen from an area. Hills make the horizon higher and can hide a low Sun. Our horizon comes from Copernicus DEM GLO-90 elevation data.
glossary.json.In Antarctica we count only 27 November: In Antarctica, we count only the time from 27 November to 1 March, when the rock maps show bare ground. We do not measure snow there.
glossary.json.A pale rock made mostly of plagioclase f: A pale rock that is mostly plagioclase feldspar. Much of the bright highland crust of the Moon is this type of rock. Our rock match looks for it.
glossary.json.A square of ground about 11 km across: t: A square of ground of approximately 11 km. It is the unit of our map and our lists. One figure gives the value for all of the area.

tour.json.On snow-free ground only 15 of them keep: On snow-free ground, only 15 of these areas keep 100 hours in the winter half.
tour.json.Typical cloud keeps a median 24 percent: Under typical cloud, the median area keeps 24 percent of those hours. 238 areas still have at least 50 hours.
tour.json.Connecting Ridge has the lowest Sun ceil: Connecting Ridge has the lowest Sun ceiling, 2.08 degrees. Its two-hour spells start only at 64.8 degrees north.
tour.json.Antarctica: snow on rock is not measured: Antarctica: we do not measure snow on rock. Thus, only the rock season counts, from 27 November to 1 March. We rank 617 areas there.
tour.json.All 11 lower-latitude analog sites lack: None of the 11 lower-latitude analog sites has a two-hour spell. For Malapert Massif, snow removes the most hours at 10 of 12 named Arctic sites.
tour.json.With reduced motion the tour waits for t: If reduced motion is on, the tour waits until the reader presses Next.
tour.json.Each step gets five seconds, and the res: Each tour stop gets 5 seconds. The page divides the rest of the minute by the length of each caption.

basis.json.Sun: our own positions, checked against: Sun: our own positions, checked against JPL Horizons. Snow: IMS satellite maps, checked at 139 weather stations. Hills: Copernicus DEM GLO-90 elevation data. Cloud: monthly means from NASA POWER.
basis.json.Sun only: our own Sun positions at 1-min: Sun only: we calculate the Sun positions at intervals of 1 minute, over a flat horizon. An independent recount differs by 0.065 hours a year or less. JPL Horizons differs by a median of 0.11 percent.
basis.json.Snow-free ground: 740 IMS satellite snow: Snow-free ground: 740 IMS satellite snow maps (daily, 4 km), from October 2015 to September 2025. We compared them with 139 weather stations.
basis.json.After terrain: each area's horizon from: After terrain: the horizon of each area comes from Copernicus DEM GLO-90 elevation data, read on a 60 m grid.
basis.json.Typical cloud: monthly mean cloud from N: Typical cloud: the monthly mean cloud from NASA POWER (CERES SYN1deg), 2001 to 2025, on a 1-degree grid of approximately 111 km.
basis.json.An area is a square about 11 km across;: An area is a square of approximately 11 km. One figure gives the value for all of the area.
basis.json.Cloud is a monthly mean over all hours o: Cloud is a monthly mean over all hours of day and night. It is not the chance that you can see a low Sun.
basis.json.Snow on Antarctic rock is not measured;: We do not measure snow on Antarctic rock. Thus, in Antarctica we count only the rock season, from 27 November to 1 March.
basis.json.Counting only spells of at least two hou: We count only spells of at least 2 hours. This is our choice, not an agency rule.
basis.json.Snow-free odds are typical for each ten-: The snow-free odds are typical values for each ten-day period from October 2015 to September 2025. They are not a forecast for one year.
basis.json.Sun heights allow for the usual bending: The Sun heights include the usual effect of the air on the direction of light (standard refraction).

meta.json.Hours count only inside unbroken spells: An hour counts only if it is in a spell of at least 2 hours without a break. We find the spells for each day separately.
meta.json.On NASA's 2022 list of 13 candidate regi: It is on the NASA list of 13 candidate regions of 2022. It is not one of the nine regions that NASA kept in 2024.

NASA Goddard studied the light on the 5 m models. This region has the most area that is in sunlight for more than 70 % of the time.

meta.json.checking the satellite snow odds against: a check of the satellite snow odds against the snow depth on the ground
meta.json.the snow maps as they read: the snow-free odds as the snow maps give them

moon.json.On the 2022 list of 13 as 'Connecting Ri: It is on the list of 13 of 2022, as 'Connecting Ridge'. It is not one of the nine regions that NASA kept in October 2024. The NASA abstract says the cut 'does not imply that removed regions are unsuitable for future exploration'.

moon.json.Candidate region; Chang'e-8 also targets: It is a candidate region. The Chang'e-8 mission also has this region as a target.
moon.json.Candidate region; most top-ranked landin: It is a candidate region. In one study, it has the most top-ranked landing points.
moon.json.1 m divided by the tangent of the Sun ce: The shadow length is 1 m divided by the tangent of the Sun ceiling, on level ground.
moon.json.An LROC NAC stereo terrain model with or: An LROC NAC stereo terrain model with orthorectified images. It is not a low-Sun mosaic. We did not check if it covers the centre of our model.
moon.json.Not computed here; compare with the NASA: We did not calculate this. Compare it with the NASA POWER temperature of each Earth place.
moon.json.Shielded by the atmosphere and the magne: The atmosphere and the magnetic field give protection.
moon.json.The same shadow length at the same Sun h: The shadow length is the same at the same Sun height. But the sky puts light into the shadow, and the air makes the low Sun darker and redder. We have no number for that difference.
moon.json.24 hours, 15° per hour: about 29.5 times: 24 hours, 15° per hour: approximately 29.5 times faster.
moon.json.Surface pressure at night about 3 x 10^-: The surface pressure at night is approximately 3 x 10^-15 bar. There is no air, no wind, no sound and no weather.
moon.json.1.62 m/s2 at the surface, about one sixt: 1.62 m/s2 at the surface, approximately one sixth of the gravity of Earth.
moon.json.Dry, sharp-grained regolith that no wate: Dry regolith with sharp grains. No water or air made the grains round. The regolith sticks to suits and equipment.
moon.json.No air and no global magnetic field to s: There is no air and no global magnetic field to stop solar particles and cosmic rays.
moon.json.One turn of the Sun around the horizon t: The Sun takes 29.53 days to go once around the horizon, approximately 0.51° per hour. A shadow stays in almost the same position for hours.
No number: we did not read a dust data set.
No number: we did not read a radiation data set.

sunpath.json.Drawn by code from JPL Horizons and Cope: Drawn by code from JPL Horizons and Copernicus elevation data. The code was written with AI assistance.
sunpath.json.The Moon's trip holds the highest Sun of: The Moon's curve shows the turn with the highest Sun of 2026. In the lunar winter, the Sun there goes down to -5.5 degrees.
sunpath.json.The Earth day is the middle of the place: The Earth day is the middle day of the best ten-day period of the place, 30 Jul-8 Aug.
sunpath.json.The grey ground belongs to the Earth pla: The grey ground is for the Earth place only.
sunpath.json.The Moon's curve assumes a smooth Moon;: The Moon's curve is for a smooth Moon. Real lunar hills hide the Sun and then show it again.
sunpath.json.The upper limit of the band, 5.55 degree: The upper limit of the band, 5.55 degrees, is the Sun ceiling from our formula. The highest Sun that we found for 2026 is 5.53 degrees.
sunpath.json.The picture matches the Sun's height onl: The picture shows only the height of the Sun. It does not show the brightness, the light from the sky or how dark the shadows are.
sunpath.json.Dots on the Moon's curve are one day apa: The dots on the Moon's curve are 1 day apart. The dots on the Earth's curve are 1 hour apart.
sunpath.json.The Earth's Sun crosses the band about 2: The Earth's Sun crosses the band approximately 29.5 times faster.
sunpath.json.The Sun moves anticlockwise at the lunar: The Sun moves anticlockwise at the lunar region and clockwise at the Earth place.
sunpath.json.The Moon's Sun is highest in the north;: The Moon's Sun is highest in the north. The Earth's Sun is lowest in the north.
sunpath.json.Most of the Earth day is off the chart:: Most of the Earth day is outside the chart, because the Sun climbs to 32 degrees at noon.
sunpath.json.The small step in the Earth curve is rea: The small break in the Earth curve is not an error. At the end of the day, the Sun is 0.25 degrees lower than at the start.
sunpath.json.A tenth of the area's points see ground: From a tenth of the points in the area, the ground is higher than 4.5 to 6.4 degrees, as a function of direction. That ground can hide a low Sun.
sunpath.json.The Earth curve includes the bending of: The Earth curve includes the effect of the air on the direction of light. The Moon has no air.
sunpath.json.At Malapert Massif the Sun takes 29.5 da: At Malapert Massif, the Sun takes 29.5 days to go once around the horizon.
sunpath.json.In the trip drawn, the one with the high: The picture shows the turn with the highest Sun of 2026. In this turn, the centre of the Sun is never higher than 5.53 degrees.
sunpath.json.At Haughton crater, Devon Island on 3 Au: At Haughton crater, Devon Island, on 3 Aug, the Sun goes once around the horizon in 1 day.
sunpath.json.It is inside the same band for 4 h 45 mi: On that day, it is inside the same band for 4 h 45 min, near midnight.

cloud_regions.json.North-west Greenland or Ellesmere is the: In July and August, North-west Greenland or Ellesmere is the clearest northern region. Its median sky cover is 65 percent, against 74 percent for all northern areas.
cloud_regions.json.Enderby and Mac.Robertson Land is the cl: In December and January, Enderby and Mac.Robertson Land is the clearest southern region. Its median sky cover is 46 percent, against 53 percent for all southern areas.
cloud_regions.json.Sky cover is a monthly mean over all hou: Sky cover is a monthly mean over all hours on a coarse grid. It is not the chance that you can see a low Sun.

airfields.json.Scheduled flights is the airport table's: The value for scheduled flights is the yes or no of the airport table. We did not compare it with a timetable.

winter_leads.json.Areas the bare-ground screen leaves out: The bare-ground screen leaves out these areas, but they have some bare ground and measured snow. They are in no ranking.
winter_leads.json.Only areas with at least 1 square km of: The list shows only areas with at least 1 square km of bare ground.
winter_leads.json.Cloud is not counted: these are hours of: We do not count cloud. These are hours of low Sun on ground that is probably free of snow. They are not hours of visible Sun.
winter_leads.json.Near a coast the snow odds rest on few l: Near a coast, the snow odds come from few land pixels of the snow maps. Each patch in the list gives the number of pixels.
winter_leads.json.Bare ground at a coast can be beach, tid: Bare ground at a coast can be beach, tidal flat, rock or a quarry. We did not find out which.
winter_leads.json.The bare area of a lead with few land-co: If a patch has few land-cover samples, the error in its bare area can be approximately as large as the bare area itself.
winter_leads.json.Areas with under 20 percent land are mis: The list does not include areas with less than 20 percent land. Thus, small islands and skerries are not in the list.
winter_leads.json.Hours after terrain exist only for the 3: Hours after terrain are available only for the 303 areas that have a terrain horizon.
winter_leads.json.Hours after terrain average over all the: Hours after terrain are a mean over all the land of an area, not over its bare ground.
winter_leads.json.North of about 67 N the winter hours fal: North of approximately 67 N, the winter hours are in October and March, not in midwinter.
winter_leads.json.Region names come from rough boxes of la: Region names come from approximate boxes of latitude and longitude. An area near a border can have the name of the region next to it.
winter_leads.json.Areas with at least that many winter hou: The number of areas in each region with at least that many winter hours, before and after terrain.
winter_leads.json.Most winter hours after terrain first; a: The list starts with the most winter hours after terrain. Areas without a terrain figure are last.

yearplan.json.Low-Sun hours after snow and terrain in: The hours of low Sun after snow and terrain, in the ten-day periods whose middle day is in the month.
yearplan.json.No entry means that no ranked area has m: If there is no entry, no ranked area has more than 5 h in that month.
yearplan.json.Only ranked areas are named: measured sn: The plan names only ranked areas. A ranked area has measured snow in the north, a terrain figure and a bare share of at least 0.25.
yearplan.json.Reachable: within 100 km of an airfield: Reachable: within 100 km of an airfield with scheduled flights. In Antarctica, within 100 km of any listed airfield.
yearplan.json.Antarctic entries carry the words 'snow: Antarctic entries show the words 'snow not measured'.
yearplan.json.In Antarctica only the rock season count: In Antarctica, only the rock season counts, from 27 November to 1 March.

rehearsal_rules.json.Checking a lamp simulator against the re: Comparison of a lamp simulator with the real Sun
rehearsal_rules.json.our rule of thumb, not an agency standar: our own rule, not an agency standard
rehearsal_rules.json.Drive one route up-sun, across the Sun a: Drive one route toward the Sun, across the Sun and away from the Sun. Then compare what the driver can see.
rehearsal_rules.json.Walk a geology traverse in low, raking l: Walk a geology traverse in low light that comes from the side.
rehearsal_rules.json.Photograph the same patch under the lamp: Photograph the same patch under the lamp and under the real low Sun at the same height. Then compare the shadows.
rehearsal_rules.json.In JETT5 the low light came from a spotl: In JETT5, the low light came from a spotlight at night. Here, the light comes from the real Sun.
rehearsal_rules.json.An unknown input is never counted as a f: The rules never count an unknown input as a fail.
rehearsal_rules.json.Each input is rounded as it is printed b: The page rounds each input as it prints it. Then it applies the rule.
rehearsal_rules.json.C and T are means over the three periods: C and T are means over the three periods. Each period uses the value of the month of its middle day.
rehearsal_rules.json.The three periods may run over the new y: The three periods can continue past the end of the year.
rehearsal_rules.json.Where the snow maps are doubtful, the lo: If the snow maps are doubtful, the rules use the lower and more cautious snow-free odds.
rehearsal_rules.json.In Antarctica the snow is not measured,: We do not measure snow in Antarctica. Thus, S is unknown there.
rehearsal_rules.json.A rule that needs S then reads 'cannot t: In that case, a rule that needs S gives 'cannot tell', unless the known inputs decide the verdict.
rehearsal_rules.json.C counts cloud over all hours of the mon: C counts cloud over all hours of the month. Thus, it tells too little about a Sun this low.
rehearsal_rules.json.When no airfield of that kind lies withi: If no airfield of that kind is within 1,500 km, D counts as more than 1,500 km.
rehearsal_rules.json.The known inputs miss both rules, whatev: The known inputs miss both rules, whatever the value of an unknown input.
rehearsal_rules.json.An input that could change the verdict i: An input that can change the verdict is unknown.

famous.json.Our rule of thumb. A step removes a site: This is our own rule. A step removes a site if no hour is left after the step. A site stays if no step removes it and its area is in the top third of ranked areas after terrain. If not, the label names the step that removes the most hours.

places.json.Not a little-known place: published spac: This is not a little-known place. Published space-analog work exists for it.
places.json.Moon and Mars: eroded 25 km impact struc: Moon and Mars: an eroded 25 km impact structure in polar desert. A report tells of an expedition in approximately 2015, with Canadian Space Agency funds and astronaut field training.
places.json.Mars: hypersaline lake that stays liquid: Mars: a hypersaline lake that stays liquid down to approximately -20 C. Scientists study its salt-loving microbes as a model for cold Martian brines.
places.json.Mars: lakes, glaciofluvial landforms and: Mars: a conference abstract with fieldwork proposes its lakes, glaciofluvial landforms and polygons as an analog for early Mars. The abstract itself calls the oasis seldom studied.
places.json.Mars: sulphate evaporites; AMASE cliff r: Mars: sulphate evaporites and AMASE rover tests on cliffs
places.json.Mars: old stromatolites and carbonates s: Mars: old stromatolites and carbonates, with samples for biosignatures (AMASE)
places.json.staffed weather station since 1933; not: A staffed weather station since 1933. It is not a research station.
places.json.research station and military base 1933: A research station and military base from 1933 to 1993. The military base is in use again. As far as we read, it is not open to visitors.
places.json.the point is the hamlet of Cambridge Bay: The point is the hamlet of Cambridge Bay.
places.json.station of the International Geophysical: A station of the International Geophysical Year 1957-58, used again in 2007-09 and now empty. The point is in the fjord. The huts are a few km away.
places.json.site of the Dutch station (wintering 196: The site of the Dutch station (a winter stay in 1968-69, summer visits to 1988, expeditions in 2015 and 2022). There is no staffed station now.
places.json.the capital's research institutions; the: The research institutions of the capital. The point is the Reykjavik weather station that our snow check uses (GHCN IC000004030).
